rows.medi_said: الواجب عندو تلات سو-- أسول-- أو-- Hold on. أسئلة.
rows.why: Inanimate objects like homework use fii- (فيو) to express containing items, not 3ind- (عندو); Amal explains at 01:11 'It doesn't have. There's in it'.
rows.english: The homework has three questions in it.

rows.amal_said: Mm-mm. Happy with me. Happy from, from something I did.
rows.why: enbese6 pairs with min (مني) for being pleased/happy with someone, not ma3 (معي / mayi); sheet: 'i feel happy / pleased because of something | Ana banbaset min'.
rows.english: You would be happy with me.

rows.medi_said: أمها أو أبوها, right? Aunts and uncles.
rows.amal_said: أوه، عمها وعمتها. Cuz ولاد أمها are أخوتها.
rows.why: He used 'her mother or father' to mean aunts and uncles instead of the words on sheet (3am / 3ammeh).

rows.medi_said: enno ana barif akhtar arabi min hom.
rows.amal_said: إشتى أنا بعرف عربي أكتر منهم.
rows.why: Prepositions attach possessive pronoun suffixes directly; min + humma is minhom (منهم), not detached 'min hom'.
rows.english: That I know more Arabic than them.

rows.why: Preposition ma3 attaches pronoun suffixes (ma3hom), not detached 'ma hom'; Amal let pass.
el-lu8a is feminine, so the predicate adjective must be feminine (muhemme, not muhim).
rows.english: They think the language is important to them.

rows.medi_said: il modara. No, modara is present...
rows.why: Amal asked for the word for 'future', he guessed modara then could not remember, and Amal supplied mustaqbal (on sheet: 'future | Musta2bal | مستقبل').

rows.medi_said: Shwe min kbar, uh, libisna costume bas kul il zgar.
rows.why: Subject is el-kbaar (the adults, 3rd person plural), so the verb must be libsu (they wore), not libisna (we wore).
rows.english: A few of the adults wore costumes.

rows.medi_said: Okay. Uh, libsa Halloween. Libsa, right?
rows.why: In idafa, a feminine noun ending in -a/-e changes to -et before the second word (libset Halloween).

rows.amal_said: لأ، عاد صغار بس حلوين قول حلوات.
rows.why: A group with boys or general plural takes the masculine/general plural adjective 7elween, not feminine plural 7elwaat.

rows.medi_said: كل حدا، آآ، جابوا واحد أكلة.
rows.amal_said: صح. بس now I'm describing one. So jab أو jabu. Cos I'm saying person.
rows.why: kul 7ada is grammatically singular, so the verb must be singular (jaab, not jaabu).

rows.medi_said: كل حدا جاب واحد أكل، أكلة. No، واحدة أكلة.
rows.amal_said: آ، واحدة is an adjective. So what do where do I put it؟
rows.why: The number wa7ad/wa7de acts as an adjective and follows the noun (akle wa7de), not before it.
6alab takes the preposition min for the person requested from (talabu minni), not a direct pronoun object on the verb.
rows.english: Her whole family requested of me.

rows.why: After a clause of requesting ('enno' expressing purpose/request 'to bring'), the verb takes present subjunctive (ajeeb), not past tense (jebet).
He asked how to say spinach in Arabic; sheet: 'spinach | sabane5 | سبانخ'.

rows.medi_said: I think it was like مختلف، قدرة مختلف.
rows.why: 5udra is feminine, so its adjective must be feminine (mu5talfeh, not mu5talef); Amal let pass.
He named Tuesday (yoam el-tulata) for Monday (yoam el-etnain); Amal said explicit 'No' and he switched.

rows.amal_said: Mm-mm. I got upset for them. And about it was I get angry.
rows.why: He used ba3asseb (engine wrote بأسب) meaning 'I get angry' for 'I got upset' (tdaaya2et / ze3elt); sheet: 'i get angry | Ana ba3asseb', 'i get upset | Ana batdaaya2'.

rows.medi_said: من الـ آخر than the end, right?
rows.amal_said: The end of it. صح، آخره.
rows.why: To say 'the end of it', attach the possessive suffix -o to aa5er (aakhro), not the definite article el- (el-aakher).
A noun with a possessive pronoun ending is already definite and can never take the prefix el-.
rows.english: I didn't like the end of it.

rows.why: 8eir (other/different) comes before the noun (8eir eshi), unlike taani which follows the noun.
rows.english: Something else / a different thing from them.

rows.medi_said: أنا قرأت الأخبار، uh, أوّل الصباح، أو بيعصبوا.
rows.why: Past continuous/state requires kaan (here kaanu for plural a5baar) before the present verb to express 'they were angering'.
7arb (war) is a hidden feminine noun, so its verb must take the 3rd feminine prefix t- (t9eer, not y9eer).
rows.english: The war is going to become worse.

rows.why: The verb et6alla3 (look at) requires the fixed preposition 3ala before its object.

rows.amal_said: Where do you put the Ls? Where is the other L? You have another L. Where do you put it?
rows.why: To mean 'the favorite thing', both the noun and the adjective need el- (el-eshi el-mufaddal); Medi repeated it without el- on eshi and Amal moved on.

rows.amal_said: التاني. Why is it ال? Because صحابك is definitive. It has a pronoun on the end.
rows.why: Because s7aabak is made definite by its possessive ending, an adjective describing it (taani/tanyeen) must take el-.

rows.medi_said: هذي أول مرة أول يومي هون.
rows.why: yawm is masculine, so the demonstrative must be hada (هذا), not hadi/hazi (هذي).
rows.english: This is my first day here.

rows.medi_said: هذي أول مرة أول يومي هون.
rows.amal_said: أول يومي is what? What does أول يومي mean?
rows.why: awal before a noun with a possessive suffix means 'the beginning of my...'; to say 'my first day', say yawmi el-awal or awal yawm eli.
